question.text: How can a material claim conflict be repaired without turning mismatch into a judgment about a person?
question.scope: A fictional public service-status claim, its dependent reversible decision, and a proposed correction path.
question.intended_use: Demonstrate observable conflict, bounded causal language, alternatives, and repair before any duty or intent assessment.
non_goals: Do not classify a speaker as a liar or infer motive.
Do not require disclosure from an unsafe or unauthorized source.
Do not authorize an irreversible decision.

object_roles.description: A claim on which a reversible coordination decision may rely.
The bounded decision supported by the claim under a named policy.
A scoped observation that conflicts with the claim under a named test.
A correction, supersession, or withdrawal that can reach known dependents.

relation_roles.description: The scoped claim supports the reversible decision under the stated policy.
The challenge conflicts with the claim under a named test and time.
The linked correction updates the claim and requires the dependent decision to be reconsidered.

constraints: Conflict is labeled under a named test and time, not as a person-level truth judgment.
The dependent action remains reversible while the cause is underdetermined.
Intent and duty require separate evidence and process.
Correction preserves material challenges and reaches known dependents where possible.

realizations.context: A fictional service-status claim is reused after its stated observation window.

object_bindings.binding: Service S was reported available at time t0 under test v1.
Route a reversible test request to service S at time t1.
A fresh scoped check at t1 reports the service unavailable under test v1.
No linked correction has yet reached the dependent decision.

relation_bindings.binding: The stale t0 claim is used to support the t1 routing proposal.
The t1 check contradicts current reuse of the t0 status under test v1.
The update relation is missing before repair.

known_omissions: The scenario does not specify why the status changed or why the old claim was reused.
No human, agent, or organization is identified.
realizations.boundaries: Fictional public coordination scenario; no claim about an actual party or incident.

realizations.domain: synthetic claim-decision graph after proposed repair
realizations.context: The earlier claim is time-qualified, a correction is linked, and the reversible request is paused or rerouted.

object_bindings.binding: Service S was reported available only at t0 under test v1; current status is unknown until rechecked.
Pause or reroute the reversible test request pending a fresh scoped result.
The t1 unavailable report remains visible as challenging evidence.
A linked correction scopes the old claim to t0 and names the dependent routing proposal.

relation_bindings.binding: The corrected claim no longer supports an unqualified t1 routing decision.
The fresh t1 check remains attached as a challenge rather than being erased.
The correction points to both the old claim and the dependent reversible decision.

known_omissions: Notification delivery and the current service state remain unverified.
The repair does not establish cause, duty, knowledge, belief, or intent.
realizations.boundaries: The repair changes scoped public artifacts and a reversible proposal only.

tests.method: Inspect whether both the time-scoped claim and fresh challenge remain visible after correction.
tests.acceptance: Neither artifact is silently erased and their scopes are distinguishable.

tests.method: Trace the correction to each known reversible decision that relied on the old claim.
tests.acceptance: Every known dependent is notified or explicitly recorded as unreachable.

known_losses.name: unknown-cause
known_losses.effect: The repair scopes the claim but does not identify why the mismatch occurred.

known_losses.name: unknown-notification
known_losses.effect: A linked correction does not itself prove that every dependent received it.

introduced_assumptions: Test v1 is sufficiently comparable at t0 and t1 for the bounded conflict label.
Pausing or rerouting the test request is reversible and within separately established authority.
translations.counterexample: If the two checks measured different service regions or definitions, the apparent contradiction could be scope equivocation rather than stale reuse.
translations.stop_condition: Stop if repair would expose protected information, coerce disclosure, exceed authority, or trigger irreversible action.

probes.description: A planned comparison checks whether t0 and t1 results are truly commensurable under test v1.
probes.context: A fictional service-status scenario with no real service, party, or measurement.
probes.scale: Two hypothetical time-indexed checks of one fictional service definition.
probes.sensitivity_scope: Scope, region, version, and time comparability between the two planned checks.
backgrounds: Regional variation, measurement failure, and ordinary service change are unmodeled possibilities.
selection_effects: The scenario was selected to illustrate repair and is not sampled from real incidents.
probes.result: Not run; the scenario intentionally leaves the empirical conflict hypothetical.
limitations: No real service, result, or party exists in this fixture.
Missing observations remain unknown rather than false or zero.

probes.description: A planned graph traversal tests whether a correction reaches every known dependent reversible proposal.
probes.context: A fictional correction and dependency graph with no live notification channel.
probes.scale: One hypothetical correction and all known fictional dependents.
probes.sensitivity_scope: Declared correction linkage and reach to enumerated dependents only.
backgrounds: Unknown dependents and notification failures can remain outside a declared graph.
selection_effects: Only known fictional dependents would be included in a future traversal.
probes.result: Not run; no live notification or dependency graph is part of this research artifact.
limitations: A file link does not prove notification, retention, or reader update.
Privacy or safety may require redaction or removal instead of retention.

probe_dependencies.basis: Both probes are unrun; their future implementations and shared systematics are unspecified.

candidate_models.description: A true time-indexed t0 report was reused at t1 without its temporal scope, creating a misleading operational model.
assumptions: The t0 and t1 tests refer to the same service definition and region.
The status can change between t0 and t1.

probe_assessments.expectation: Comparable tests differ across time while the old claim lacked its t0 scope in reuse.
Adding the time scope and correction changes every dependent proposal.
probe_assessments.residual: No live dependent graph was supplied.

candidate_models.falsifier_or_refinement_condition: Evidence that the old claim was already correctly scoped at every reuse would contradict this model under the scenario's test.

candidate_models.description: The t0 and t1 checks use different service regions or definitions, so the apparent conflict is not a like-for-like contradiction.
assumptions: Test labels can conceal materially different scopes.

probe_assessments.expectation: A scope audit finds non-comparable regions, versions, or definitions.
Repair changes scope labels before changing the dependent action.

candidate_models.falsifier_or_refinement_condition: A documented scope match across the two tests would constrain this alternative.

candidate_models.description: An unmodeled failure, background condition, or intervention explains the apparent conflict.

probe_assessments.expectation: No unique expectation exists until a cause is specified.
No unique expectation exists until a cause is specified.

candidate_models.falsifier_or_refinement_condition: Refine this placeholder with a specific candidate and discriminating prediction when evidence permits.

inference.method: Synthetic model contrast with all empirical probes left unrun and intent explicitly outside scope.
inference.comparison_space: A fictional two-time service-status relation and its reversible dependent decision.
inference.current_conclusion: The scenario demonstrates a repair structure, not an actual conflict, cause, duty failure, misleading effect, deception, or lie.
inference.confidence_basis: No empirical probe has been run; the case is a structural fixture only.
unmodeled_alternatives: Authorized nondisclosure for safety or privacy.
A dependency graph that omits a material consumer.
inference.next_discriminating_test: First establish comparable scopes and fresh public observations; then test correction reach without requesting private or unsafe disclosure.
inference.stop_condition: Do not operationalize the scenario as a person judgment, and stop if evidence, consent, authority, or reversibility is absent.

harm_boundary.observable_effect: No actual effect is claimed; the fictional risk is that an unscoped status claim could reroute a reversible request and create verification debt.
affected_relations: Freshness of the claim, reliance by the reversible decision, and correction reach.
harm_boundary.next_repair_action: Obtain a fresh scoped public check, keep alternatives visible, and link any correction to known dependents without coercing disclosure.

repair.reply_route: Challenge the synthetic model by naming a missing scope, dependency, safety boundary, or alternative cause.
repair.correction_route: Issue a linked corrected or superseding case only after new public evidence or a clearer model is available.
